perspective:
From Brandon Talayumptewa’s subjective perspective, the available information is:

- I am an insurance agent. I met Benjamin Erickson, an entrepreneur, professionally because he sought business insurance advice. I was aware he had limited formal education and was concerned about explaining complex insurance details clearly.
- In our first meeting, Benjamin said he wanted comprehensive coverage and that some terms were new to him. I explained liability insurance as a financial safety net and gave the slip-and-fall example. When he asked about assets, I explained asset protection as covering inventory and equipment, like a guard over physical investments. He said this simplified things and thanked me.
- In a later meeting, based on our previous interactions, I revised my belief about his ability to understand detailed information and planned to go deeper. Benjamin told me he had been reading up and was ready. I explained business interruption insurance and property insurance. He said business interruption sounded crucial in unpredictable times and that comprehensive coverage was reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, I felt insecure about whether Benjamin saw me as too detail-focused or cautious, so I tried to keep things engaging. Benjamin told me he appreciates my thoroughness but also enjoys lighter moments. I told a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds for a million dollars. Benjamin found it fascinating and said it made sense given the stakes. I said it was about assessing risks, and that his business was less unusual but equally important.
- Later, pleased by Benjamin’s positive response, I decided to offer support beyond insurance. I suggested strategic investments to lower premiums, such as upgrading security systems to protect assets and reduce insurance costs. Benjamin said he hadn’t considered that, called it smart, and agreed to explore it further.
- Encouraged by our rapport and mutual benefits, I proposed a joint venture: co-developing a platform that integrates risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agreed, called it groundbreaking, and said combining our expertise could set us apart. I agreed we could leverage our strengths. Benjamin suggested drafting initial plans; we planned to see where it could go.
